adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test] tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py (TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe) — mock occurrence uses group_key="val1" but expected DetectorEvaluationResult uses "group_key"; the fingerprint mismatch makes the assertion inconsistent; fixture should use the same group key in both places

adjudication.rationale: In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe`, the fixture builds `occurrence, event_data = build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...)` but then constructs `expected_result = DetectorEvaluationResult("group_key", ...)` (and the subsequent `evaluate_group_key_value(...)` call is expected to be for that same `"group_key"`). Since `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` uses the provided `group_key` to compute the occurrence fingerprint via `handler.build_fingerprint(group_key)`, the expected `occurrence`/`event_data` will not correspond to the `group_key` in the expected result, making the assertion inconsistent and likely failing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test] tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py (build_mock_occurrence_and_event) — hardcoded id="eb4b0acffadb4d098d48cb14165ab578" and event_id="43878ab4419f4ab181f6379ac376d5aa" mean every occurrence shares identical ids, masking collision/dedup bugs and weakening assert_has_calls verification; ids should be derived per call (e.g., from the group key)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added test helper `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` (tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py), the `IssueOccurrence` is constructed with hardcoded `id="eb4b0acffadb4d098d48cb14165ab578"` and `event_id="43878ab4419f4ab181f6379ac376d5aa"`. This is diff-grounded and can reduce the test’s ability to detect bugs related to uniqueness/collision/deduplication of occurrences across multiple evaluations, since multiple produced occurrences will share identical identifiers regardless of `group_key`. It’s not a production defect, but it is a concrete test-quality concern introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test] tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py (BaseDetectorHandlerTest.setUp/tearDown) — patcher entered manually via __enter__() and exited in tearDown; if setUp raises after __enter__, tearDown never runs and the StatusChangeMessage.__eq__ patch leaks into other tests; use self.addCleanup(self.sm_comp_patcher.__exit__, None, None, None)

adjudication.rationale: In `BaseDetectorHandlerTest.setUp`, the patcher is started via `self.sm_comp_patcher.__enter__()` and only stopped in `tearDown` via `__exit__`. If `setUp` raises after `__enter__()` (e.g., during the inline `GroupType`/handler class definitions or other setup work), `tearDown` will not run and the `StatusChangeMessage.__eq__` patch can leak into other tests. Using `addCleanup(self.sm_comp_patcher.__exit__, None, None, None)` (or `self.sm_comp_patcher.start()` with `addCleanup(self.sm_comp_patcher.stop)`) would make cleanup robust.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py (evaluate_group_key_value) — PriorityLevel(new_status) performs an unguarded enum cast on a condition-derived value; any status value without a PriorityLevel equivalent raises ValueError mid-evaluation, failing the entire detector batch instead of skipping that group key; worth a guard or explicit mapping

adjudication.rationale: In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` the new non-OK branch now does `PriorityLevel(new_status)` before calling `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)`. `new_status` is a `DetectorPriorityLevel` derived from workflow condition results, and this cast is unguarded (no try/except or explicit mapping). If a condition result ever contains a value that `PriorityLevel` doesn’t define, Python will raise `ValueError` and abort evaluation/processing rather than skipping that group key. The diff doesn’t prove the enums currently diverge, but the risk is real and introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py — only the occurrence-producing (non-OK) path is verified end-to-end through process_detectors/produce_occurrence_to_kafka; there is no equivalent test asserting an OK transition produces a StatusChangeMessage payload (payload_type=PayloadType.STATUS_CHANGE) via process_detectors, leaving the resolve path's Kafka payload untested

adjudication.rationale: In the updated tests, end-to-end Kafka production is asserted only for the non-OK path: `TestProcessDetectors.test_state_results` and `test_state_results_multi_group` patch `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` and verify `payload_type=PayloadType.OCCURRENCE` with `status_change=None`. The OK/resolve path is exercised only at the handler level (e.g. `TestEvaluate.test_above_below_threshold` asserts `DetectorEvaluationResult.result` is a `StatusChangeMessage`), but there is no corresponding `process_detectors(...)` test that patches `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` and asserts a `PayloadType.STATUS_CHANGE` payload is produced when `new_status == DetectorPriorityLevel.OK` (see `evaluate_group_key_value`, which builds a `StatusChangeMessage` for OK and `process_detectors` which calls `create_issue_occurrence_from_result` for any non-None result). This is a specific test gap for the resolve path’s Kafka emission after the refactor to dict-based results.
